q: where the LORD appeared to David his father

s: LORD's temple has length sixty cubits (after the first measure)
q: the length by cubits after the first measure was sixty cubits, and the width twenty cubits.

s: LORD's temple has width twenty cubits
q: the length by cubits after the first measure was sixty cubits, and the width twenty cubits.

s: LORD's temple has part porch (front of the house) (twenty cubits long across the width of the house, height one hundred twenty)
q: The porch that was in front, its length, across the width of the house, was twenty cubits, and the height one hundred twenty

s: LORD's temple has part larger room (of the house) (ceiling of cypress wood overlaid with fine gold, ornamented with palm trees and chains)
q: He made the larger room with a ceiling of cypress wood, which he overlaid with fine gold, and ornamented it with palm trees and chains.

s: LORD's temple is decorated with precious stones (for beauty)
q: He decorated the house with precious stones for beauty.

s: Hezekiah appoints priests (into divisions, each according to his service)
q: Hezekiah appointed the divisions of the priests and the Levites after their divisions, every man according to his service

s: Conaniah rules over tithes and first fruits (offerings) (ruler over the offerings, tithes, and dedicated things)
q: They brought in the offerings, the tithes, and the dedicated things faithfully. Conaniah the Levite was ruler over them

s: Conaniah has brother Shimei (Shimei was second)
q: Conaniah the Levite was ruler over them, and Shimei his brother was second.

s: Israel destroys pillars (broke them in pieces)
q: all Israel who were present went out to the cities of Judah and broke the pillars in pieces

s: Israel destroys Asherah poles (cut them down)
q: cut down the Asherah poles

s: Israel destroys high places and altars (idolatrous objects) (throughout Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim and Manasseh)
q: broke down the high places and the altars out of all Judah and Benjamin, also in Ephraim and Manasseh, until they had destroyed them all

s: Israel gives tithes and first fruits (offerings) (abundantly)
q: the children of Israel gave in abundance the first fruits of grain, new wine, oil, honey, and of all the increase of the field; and they brought in the tithe of all things abundantly.

s: Judah has inhabitants who give tithes and first fruits (offerings) (tithe of cattle and sheep and dedicated things)
q: The children of Israel and Judah, who lived in the cities of Judah, also brought in the tithe of cattle and sheep, and the tithe of dedicated things which were consecrated to the LORD their God

s: heaps (of offerings) holds tithes and first fruits (offerings) (tithe of cattle, sheep and dedicated things laid in heaps)
q: and laid them in heaps.

s: heaps (of offerings) has construction period third to seventh month
q: In the third month, they began to lay the foundation of the heaps, and finished them in the seventh month.

s: priests receives tithes and first fruits (offerings) (portion given by people of Jerusalem so they may devote themselves to the law)
q: he commanded the people who lived in Jerusalem to give the portion of the priests and the Levites, that they might give themselves to the LORD’s law.

s: Hezekiah appoints Levites (into divisions, each according to his service)
q: Hezekiah appointed the divisions of the priests and the Levites after their divisions, every man according to his service

s: Levites receives tithes and first fruits (offerings) (portion given by people of Jerusalem so they may devote themselves to the law)
q: he commanded the people who lived in Jerusalem to give the portion of the priests and the Levites, that they might give themselves to the LORD’s law.

s: Hezekiah is a king
q: by the appointment of Hezekiah the king and Azariah the ruler of God’s house

s: Hezekiah provides burnt offerings (king's portion of his possessions, for morning and evening, Sabbaths, new moons and set feasts)
q: He also appointed the king’s portion of his possessions for the burnt offerings: for the morning and evening burnt offerings, and the burnt offerings for the Sabbaths, for the new moons, and for the set feasts

s: Hezekiah has character good, right, and faithful (before the LORD his God)
q: he did that which was good, right, and faithful before the LORD his God.

s: Hezekiah serves LORD (seeks his God with all his heart and prospers)
q: In every work that he began in the service of God’s house, in the law, and in the commandments, to seek his God, he did it with all his heart and prospered.

s: Azariah is a chief priest (of the house of Zadok)
q: Azariah the chief priest, of the house of Zadok

s: Azariah is a ruler of God’s house
q: Azariah the ruler of God’s house

s: Conaniah is a Levite
q: Conaniah the Levite was ruler over them

s: Sennacherib is a king of Assyria
q: Sennacherib king of Assyria came, entered into Judah

s: Hezekiah has acts recorded in book of the kings of Judah and Israel (also in the vision of Isaiah)
q: the rest of the acts of Hezekiah and his good deeds, behold, they are written in the vision of Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.

s: Hezekiah has status exalted in the sight of all nations (after the deliverance)
q: so that he was exalted in the sight of all nations from then on.

s: Hezekiah redirected Gihon (upper spring brought down west of David's city)
q: This same Hezekiah also stopped the upper spring of the waters of Gihon, and brought them straight down on the west side of David’s city.

s: Sennacherib attacks Lachish (with all his forces)
q: now he was attacking Lachish, and all his forces were with him

s: Sennacherib killed by Sennacherib's sons (in the house of his god)
q: those who came out of his own body killed him there with the sword.

s: Sennacherib worships Sennacherib's god
q: When he had come into the house of his god

s: Hezekiah is a king of Judah
q: Hezekiah king of Judah

s: Sennacherib's letters insults LORD (God of Israel)
q: He also wrote letters insulting the LORD, the God of Israel, and speaking against him

s: LORD is god of Israel
q: the LORD, the God of Israel

s: Assyrian siege of Jerusalem has outcome Assyrian forces cut off by angel; Sennacherib returned in shame (the LORD saved Jerusalem)
q: The LORD sent an angel, who cut off all the mighty men of valor, the leaders, and captains in the camp of the king of Assyria. So he returned with shame of face to his own land.

s: LORD saves Jerusalem (from Sennacherib)
q: Thus the LORD saved Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib the king of Assyria

s: Babylon sent ambassadors of the princes of Babylon (to inquire of the wonder in the land)
q: concerning the ambassadors of the princes of Babylon, who sent to him to inquire of the wonder that was done in the land

s: Manasseh is a king of Judah (succeeded Hezekiah)
q: Manasseh his son reigned in his place.

s: Hezekiah worships LORD (his God)
q: the LORD our God is with us to help us and to fight our battles

s: Hezekiah has son Manasseh (successor as king)
q: Manasseh his son reigned in his place.

s: Hezekiah has burial place ascent to the tombs of the sons of David
q: they buried him in the ascent to the tombs of the sons of David

s: Hezekiah has wealth exceedingly great riches and honor (given by God)
q: Hezekiah had exceedingly great riches and honor.

s: Hezekiah owns treasuries, storehouses, stalls, cities, flocks and herds
q: He provided himself with treasuries for silver, for gold, for precious stones, for spices, for shields, and for all kinds of valuable vessels;

s: Hezekiah removed high places and altars (commanded worship at one altar)
q: Hasn’t the same Hezekiah taken away his high places and his altars, and commanded Judah and Jerusalem, saying, ‘You shall worship before one altar, and you shall burn incense on it’?

s: Hezekiah is associated with Isaiah (prayed together with the prophet)
q: Hezekiah the king and Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, prayed because of this, and cried to heaven.

s: Manasseh is a king (reigned in Jerusalem)
q: Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem.

s: Manasseh practiced child sacrifice (Manasseh's children passed through fire) (in the valley of the son of Hinnom)
q: He also made his children to pass through the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom.

s: Manasseh set up idol (Manasseh's engraved image) (in God’s house)
q: He set the engraved image of the idol, which he had made, in God’s house

s: Manasseh seduced Judah (to do more evil than the nations)
q: Manasseh seduced Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that they did more evil than did the nations whom the LORD destroyed before the children of Israel.

s: Manasseh was taken captive by Assyrian army captains (carried to Babylon in chains)
q: the LORD brought on them the captains of the army of the king of Assyria, who took Manasseh in chains, bound him with fetters, and carried him to Babylon.

s: Manasseh’s captivity and repentance occurs in Babylon (Manasseh carried there)
q: carried him to Babylon.

s: Manasseh’s captivity and repentance results in humility before God (Manasseh begged the LORD in distress)
q: When he was in distress, he begged the LORD his God, and humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers.

s: Manasseh knows LORD (learned that the LORD was God after restoration)
q: Then Manasseh knew that the LORD was God.
